sla_requirements: Target uptime: customer requests 99.99% for critical inference endpoints (prefer 99.995% for leaderboards); Redwood initial offer 99.95% for Dedicated
Credit schedule requested: tiered - 99.9-99.95% => 5% monthly credit; 99.5-99.9% => 15% credit; <99.5% => 40% credit (customer wants higher floor)
Maintenance windows: customer requires maintenance only in 02:00-05:00 PT monthly window for production; cannot accept multi-hour unscheduled maintenance during business hours
Support response times: Sev1 (production down) - 15 minute phone acknowledgement, 1 hour initial remediation; Sev2 - 1 hour acknowledgement, 4 hour action plan; 24/7 phone escalation required
Throughput guarantees: reserved baseline capacity to sustain 200 requests/sec (avg payload) during business hours with burst to 400 rps for 30 minutes; need per-route throughput SLAs
Latency SLOs: p50 generation <150ms, p95 <700ms for 128-token completions; require measurable P95 telemetry and token-level tracing for regressions

Scaling & reserved GPU planning: initial commit = 4x 80GB GPUs (A100-equivalent) for primary cluster, burst pool to 8 GPUs; dedicated autoscaling policy with guaranteed warm workers for prefix caching
Fallback policy: when primary capacity exhausted, automatic routing to cheaper model variant (must preserve SLA for critical routes) - customer wants explicit rules
Monitoring & reporting: weekly latency/cost report + daily outage summary within 1 hour of incident start; raw traces shared for postmortems
Data residency & retention mapping in SLA: logs and KV caches must be in US region by default for Trident customers
